title: F1,6BP in WWOX-LoF
summary: Fructose-1,6-bisphosphate tests a rapid calcium effect and a delayed change in glucose use.

graph.evidence: Juvenile rat slices show smaller calcium and GABA currents.
graph.inference: Free ions and circuit inhibition constrain interpretation.
graph.hypothesis: A separate glucose-flux effect may follow in defined WWOX cells.
graph.experiment: Match free ions and activity, then trace glucose and read function.

evidence: In juvenile CA3, nominal bath exposure suppressed bursts in 13 of 19 slices. Peak calcium current fell 39.8% and evoked GABA current fell 48.2% in separate recordings.
In a juvenile rat status model, 6 of 10 animals in the higher exposure arm stopped electrographic and behavioral status. Acute provoked status is the setting of the observation.
inference: The Wwox-null fibroblast F1,6BP pool was higher in the published panel. The held neural RNA datasets showed preparation-dependent changes in carbon-handling transcripts. Neither measures pathway flux.
hypothesis: A rapid extracellular effect and a slower metabolic contribution can coexist. Reduced activity can itself change isotope labeling and energetic demand.
experiment: Restore measured free calcium and magnesium and match recruitment. Read recurrence and inhibitory function before testing a delayed genotype-dependent tracer and redox effect at matched activity.
limits: Total adult rat blood and brain homogenate cannot establish free juvenile brain exposure. Keep as a conditional local research comparator and defer systemic pediatric WWOX priority.
